title: Signal synthesis ontology and procurement decision rulebook for model sourcing
creator: Ethan Brooks
description:
Goal: Produce an operational ontology (taxonomy) of competitive signals for model sourcing and a small, human-readable decision rulebook that procurement/product teams can use to trigger vendor engagement or model rollouts.

Background: We have dozens of market intelligence artifacts (benchmarks, pricing sheets, telemetry, partner notes) but no unified structure for turning those signals into deterministic operational actions (e.g., when to trial a new quantized model for embeddings, when to escalate to sales for Dedicated capacity). That gap causes delayed responses to changes in model availability, price shifts, and emergent capability gaps.

Scope:
- In-scope: Competitive signals that affect sourcing and serving economics (latency, cost per token/embedding, availability, quantization compatibility), capability regressions (quality on prompt suites), and contractual/region constraints (compliance, data residency).
- Out-of-scope: Deep model architecture research (LLM internals), long-term procurement negotiation playbooks.

Success criteria (MVP):
1) A published signal taxonomy (CSV + short confluence page) with: signal name, measurement method, data source, refresh cadence, confidence band, recommended action (probe / schedule capacity / no-op).
2) Decision rulebook with 10 deterministic rules mapping signal thresholds to actions (e.g., if regional-serving-latency > 250ms and avg-cost-per-1k-tokens increases > 12% -> open Capacity Alert ticket to ENG and Sales).
3) Ingest spec for two telemetry sources (token-cost telemetry + availability feed) and a prototype ingestion lambda + sample dataset (first 30 days).
4) One evaluation harness with 6 representative prompts for quality drift checks and a baseline scoring script.
5) Stakeholder sign-off (PM, SRE, Procurement) and a small-run experiment to surface 2 real procurement triggers in Q2.

Deliverables:
- sources/pm/signal-taxonomy-CSV (master list) + confluence doc link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PM/pages/Signal+Synthesis+Ontology
- Ingest spec (owner: Data Eng), GH stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/signal-ingest/pull/1204
- Decision rulebook PDF (one-pager) + Jira/Linear runbook entries to automate basic thresholds
- Evaluation harness: repo at https://github.com/redwood-inference/evals/tree/mvp-signal-harness

Stakeholders: PM (Sophie Kramer), Data Eng (Amina Patel), SRE (Leo Nguyen), Procurement lead (Maya Singh), Research (Dr. Daniel Park).

Risks & trade-offs:
- Overfitting rules to current vendors: mitigate by adding automatic expiry (90 days) and a review cadence.
- Noisy telemetry causing false positives: include confidence band and minimum sample size in each rule.
- Scope creep into full procurement automation: keep MVP limited to alerts and manual follow-up.

Timeline & milestones:
- 2026-03-01: Kickoff and initial taxonomy draft (done).
- 2026-03-08: Telemetry ingest spec + prototype lambda (data eng sprint).
- 2026-03-12: Draft decision rules and internal review (current).
- 2026-03-25: Run first-week experiment and capture 2 triggers.
- 2026-04-02: Final sign-off and handoff to Signals Ops for continuous ingestion.

Next steps:
1) Finalize taxonomy CSV and push to confluence.
2) Data Eng to finish ingest lambda and deliver sample dataset for March.
3) Research to run baseline scoring on the 6 prompts and upload results to the evals repo.
4) Schedule stakeholder review (Sophie to book).
